note: Endpoints this app serves that the pack's agent API (agent_api/endpoints.json) does not have yet. tools/export_mcp_catalog.py adds them to the tool catalog, endpoints.md and the OpenAPI file. When the pack gets the same route, delete its entry here so the pack's own is used.

endpoints.description: The overlay library: `items` (clips to overlay, each with `id`, `category`, `duration`, size and `suggested_blend`), `fonts` (names a text clip's `font` can use), `luts` (installed .cube files for a LUT clip), `caption_styles` (clean, bold, lower) and `kinds` (media, grain, vignette, text, lut). The person fills the library in the app (Post Process, Overlays). Use an item's `id` with POST /projects/{pid}/overlay-layers/media.

The project's overlays as the render sees it: `overlay_layer_track` (`enabled`), `overlay_layers` (every setting filled in and clamped), `count`, `revision`, and `warnings` for layers that will not draw as asked (a missing media file, a LUT or font that is not installed, an unknown kind, empty text). Overlays are drawn onto the final video by the stitch (`stitch_final`, `pipeline_build_full_video`) and by the Video Builder's Render All and Export. The timeline is in seconds from the start of the song.

Replace the project's overlays (`overlay_layers`, the whole list) and/or the switch for all of them (`overlay_layer_track`, `{"enabled": false}` turns every overlay off for every render without deleting the layers). Read first (GET), change what you need, send the list back. Later layers draw on top. Every layer has `kind` (media, grain, vignette, text, lut), `id`, `start` and `end` in seconds, `enabled`, `locked`, `opacity` (0 to 1), `fade_in` and `fade_out` (seconds). media: `path` (a file in the project, `overlay/<name>`, from POST /projects/{pid}/overlay-layers/media), `blend_mode` (screen drops black and suits dust, smoke and flares, then add, lighten, overlay, softlight, multiply, normal), `scale` (cover, contain, stretch), `loop`, `speed` (0.5 to 2), `flip_h`, `brightness` (-1 to 1), `contrast` (0 to 2), `tint` (#rrggbb). grain: `strength` (0 to 60, 20 to 30 is film), `chroma` (0 to 20), `size` (fine, medium, coarse), `animated`. vignette: `strength` (0 to 1, 0.7 is the default). text: `text`, `font`, `size` (pixels on a 1080 tall picture), `color`, `outline_width`, `outline_color`, `shadow`, `x` and `y` (0 to 1, the centre of the text), `animation` (none or slide_up). lut: `lut` (an installed .cube name), `strength` (0 to 1). Values out of range are clamped and the reply shows what was saved. A clip sent without `locked` is unlocked. Send If-Match with the revision you read.

Add `layers` (a list of overlay layers, fields as in PUT /projects/{pid}/overlay-layers) to the end of the list without touching the others. The reply is the whole list with `added`, the ids the new layers got.

Add one text clip for each lyric line, timed to the words of the song when the project has word timing (`project_context/timestamped_lyrics.json`, from the lyrics alignment) and otherwise one caption over each scene that has lyrics. `style` is clean (default), bold or lower (a lower third). `from` and `to` (seconds) limit it to a range. Captions from an earlier run are replaced (only those inside the range when one is given) unless `replace` is false. The reply is the whole list with `source` (timestamped_lyrics or scenes), `style` and `captions`.

Add a clip of the overlay library (`library_id`, from GET /overlay-library) as an overlay: it is copied into the project's `overlay` folder and starts at `start` (default 0) and runs to `end` (default the end of the timeline, looping its file). The blend mode is the library's suggestion (screen for clips on black). Any other media clip field (opacity, blend_mode, speed, fades) can be sent too. The reply is the whole list with `added` and the project `path`.
